assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED turned a superconducting artificial atom coupled to a microwave resonator into a controllable platform: strong coupling, dispersive readout, and the transmon-era toolbox. It is a clean case where a basic quantum phenomenon became visible and controllable on a chip, and it is the natural continuation of the 2025 prize on macroscopic tunnelling in circuits. Its originality and lasting impact on microwave quantum optics are very high.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the first strong-coupling experiment (Wallraff et al.) are tightly linked. Blais for theory, Wallraff and Schoelkopf for experiment is a defensible trio. Girvin is not in the credited names, so his role in the proposal cannot be recognized here. I work in this field, so I flag a possible conflict of interest and a risk of overweighting it.
assessment.maturity: Strong-coupling results have been reproduced in many laboratories for two decades, and the framework underlies essentially all superconducting-qubit readout and gates. Recognition is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Possible conflict of interest given my own field and WACQT role.
Credit split between theory proposal and the first experiments, and Girvin's absence from the credited names.
From memory, I have not independently verified exact dates and author contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with magic-wavelength trapping, brought systematic uncertainty to the 1e-18 level and opened precision tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. It is a clean, controllable quantum-optics achievement with unambiguous measurable impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and built early clocks, and Ye's group drove the record accuracy and many-body clock advances. Two laureates is a clean configuration, though Ye already shares the 2005 prize (frequency combs), which the committee may weigh, and ion clocks (Wineland) are already recognized.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across several laboratories (JILA, RIKEN, PTB, NIST, SYRTE) and a stable interpretation. Redefinition of the second is still pending, but the science is mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior prizes for frequency combs and ion clocks.
Others, such as Lemonde, Ludlow or Schiller, might be argued for credit; I cannot verify from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect opened a new class of quantum matter, with a theory prediction (Z2 invariant) confirmed by clear transport experiments in HgTe. Original, conceptually deep and broadly influential.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele for the Z2 theory, Molenkamp for the experimental HgTe observation (with Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang theory, not credited here). Hasan is a fourth name, so the three-person limit forces a choice, and I choose the theory plus the clear transport demonstration. The set is imperfect because BHZ's HgTe prediction is not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many materials by transport and ARPES, with a stable interpretation. Recognition is timely, though some may regard it as part of the earlier topology theme.
uncertainties: Allocation among four credited names is contested and omits Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang.
Outside my main expertise; I defer partly to condensed-matter colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed the trapped-ion quantum gate and, with the ensuing quantum-simulation program, laid the theoretical basis for controlled many-body quantum systems with atoms and ions. It is foundational and was followed by decisive experiments.
assessment.attribution: Two theorists with a clear joint credit; the ion-gate experiments (Wineland, Blatt, Monroe) are by others, partly already recognized in 2012. The credit of the theory itself is cleanly shared.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally validated for 30 years, and the ideas are central to quantum computing and simulation. Timely, with some risk that the committee wants experiments included.
uncertainties: The prize might need to be paired with experimental work, which is not within the credited names.
Overlap with candidate B016 on atomic quantum simulation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light for interferometry, from Caves's quantum-noise analysis to demonstration of squeezing and its use in gravitational-wave detectors, is a clear case of quantum optics enabling a measurement beyond the standard quantum limit.
assessment.attribution: Caves for the 1981 theory, Kimble for the first squeezing experiments, and Schnabel for the GEO600 and later detector squeezing; Mavalvala is a fourth name and the choice is arguable. Credit for the early squeezing experiments (Slusher and collaborators) is not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Squeezing is routine in LIGO and Virgo, so it is mature and robust, though the GW detection prize in 2017 already rewarded much of the field.
uncertainties: Credit omits the first squeezing experimentalists.
Choice between Mavalvala and Schnabel is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg-blockade arrays of tweezers-trapped atoms provide programmable quantum simulators and emerging quantum processors, with a new regime of controllable many-body physics. The scientific idea and results are strong.
assessment.attribution: Saffman and Lukin for Rydberg-blockade gate proposals, Browaeys and Lukin for experimental arrays; Jaksch, Zoller and Weiss and others are not credited, so the allocation is unclear.
assessment.maturity: Fast-moving, with many recent results and platform competition. It is somewhat early for a prize.
uncertainties: Technology still evolving, and error-correction milestones are recent.
Incomplete credit set among Rydberg-blockade pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Higgs discovery completed the Standard Model and is a landmark confirmation after half a century. Its significance is beyond doubt.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognized the theory. The experiments are large collaborations, and the statutes allow at most three individuals, so picking spokespersons and founders is difficult and possibly unfair. Four credited names are available, and I select three; Della Negra is a hard omission.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by two experiments with a stable interpretation. Timing is long-delayed, though recognition remains valid.
uncertainties: Attribution to individuals in large collaborations is the main obstacle.
Particle physics is outside my expertise, so I defer to colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy by detecting a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the association with the blazar TXS 0506+056. This is an important new window on the universe.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the project and its concept, and Karle and Spiering are central early figures. As with other large collaborations, attribution to individuals is delicate.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is well established, though source identification is still developing and independent confirmation (KM3NeT, Baikal) is limited.
uncertainties: Source identification is incomplete, and the interpretation may still change.
Astroparticle physics is outside my expertise.
